messages:
incident-bot: Pager: GPU ECC error rate spike on cluster-prod (alert: gpu_node_ecc_rate_high). Paged @oncall @eng-sre.

maria: seeing a big spike on node-gpu-42 and node-gpu-43, ECC corrected errors jumped to ~120/5m on node-gpu-42. Prom query: `increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m])`

alex: confirmed, also noticing short VRAM pressure on node-gpu-43 (gpu_memory_used_bytes / gpu_memory_total_bytes ~ 0.92 for bursts). Latency for chat-inference-prod routes spiked to 600ms and a few 429s.

sam: I’m putting node-gpu-42 into drain to stop more jobs landing: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-42 && kubectl drain node-gpu-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

karen: on it — moving small percentage of traffic to dedicated-reserve pool and switching fallback to model: `redwood request route set --route chat-prod --model small-gpt-v1 --weight 100` to reduce load.

jordan: attaching current logs and sensor traces: `/var/log/nvidia/driver.log` shows repeated ECC corrected messages around 11:12:03. Also node shows thermal ramp from 72C -> 88C over ~4 minutes.

maria: suspected recent driver restart earlier today? I see a rolling node reboot at 03:40 that touched the same nodes; might be sensor mis-calibration after driver update.

incident-bot: Acknowledged by maria. Escalation to eng-sre in 30m if > 10 ECC errors/min persists or new nodes start flapping.

alex: mitigation status: node-gpu-42 drained, pods rescheduled on reserved pool; no new ECC spikes for 3m on remaining nodes. Traffic steady, latency returning to baseline (~120ms). No customers reported errors yet but we had a couple 429s during spike window.

sam: putting temporary suppression on the pager for gpu_node_ecc_rate_high for 20m while we triage (silence id: s-2345). Leaving metric alert visible in dashboard only.

karen: creating a quick dashboard panel (grafana) for ops: `ops/gpu-health` w/ panels: ECC corrected per-node, GPU temp, VRAM usage histogram, and node drain history. Query sample we used: `sum by (node) (increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m]))` and `max by(node) (nvidia_gpu_temp_celsius)`

maria: root-cause hypothesis: transient ECC corrections driven by thermal spike after driver re-init plus a couple long-running jobs squeezing VRAM — sensors produce bursts that look like faults. Not seeing raw uncorrected ECC errors (which would be true hardware failure).

jordan: agreed. Next steps: add a 2m `for` clause to the ECC alert and increase threshold to reduce flapping pages. Current alert: `gpu_node_ecc_rate_high > 5` (per 1m) — propose change to `> 20` over 3m aggregated, or `for: 2m` depending on sensitivity. Also add composite condition: only page if ECC > 20 AND gpu_temp_celsius > 85 OR vrm_memory_pressure > 0.9.

alex: action items (quick):
- change alert rule: set `for: 2m` and change threshold to `20` (maria)
- add composite check so we don't page on sensor noise (jordan)
- publish new grafana dashboard and pin in runbook (karen)
- update runbook with drain command & fallback model playbook (sam)
- schedule sensor/driver validation on next maintenance window (alex)

maria: editing alert now in prometheus:
```
- alert: gpu_node_ecc_rate_high
  expr: sum by(node) (increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m])) > 20
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU ECC corrected errors high on {{ $labels.node }}"
```

maria: also creating a non-paging slack-only alert for moderate ECC bursts to feed into ops channel (`severity: ticket`) so we get visibility without waking oncall.

sam: added temp/vrm composite alert: `gpu_node_critical_combo` — pages only if `(increase(ecc[5m]) > 20 AND max(temp[5m]) > 85) OR (vrm_mem_util > 0.95)`. I’ll PR the rules.

karen: dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/gpu-health?orgId=1 (pinned to runbook). I added the VRAM heatmap and an ECC sparklines row per node.

jordan: note for postmortem: customer-impact window ~ 11:11–11:17 UTC, small spike in 429s on chat-inference-prod and slight latency increase for high-concurrency requests. No data leak or model corruption.

maria: closing the pager in 30m unless we see recurrence. Logging follow-up to incident tracker (INC-2026-314).

alex: post-incident follow-ups assigned in ticket: driver validation, long-running-job scheduling to avoid sustained VRAM pressure, and update alert thresholds with test in staging.

sam: thumbs: :thumbsup: — will draft a short postmortem blurb and schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to review telemetry and finalize thresholds.

karen: added note to runbook: new drain command + check list -> `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-gpu-42` and verify replicas and persistent state before drain.

incident-bot: Incident stable. Pager closed by maria. Next automated follow-up reminder in 24h to validate driver metrics in staging.

maria: thanks everyone — great quick coordination. We avoided replacing hardware by tuning alerts and draining nodes quickly.

alex: marking thread solved.
